```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Idea B's core feature, description generation, is free in Shopify Magic for every paid-plan merchant, and B's own brief calls this a major threat. That leaves only the alt-text, bulk and vision use cases as paid ground, and AltText.ai already holds that ground with 141 reviews and a Built for Shopify badge. Idea A's brief names no free built-in substitute. Registered agents and accountants appear only as an open question, not as evidence.",
    "A's need recurs by nature: renewal cycles, audit dates and rule changes keep coming. B's brief says its need may be one-time per catalog. That matters for converting a trial into a paying subscriber and keeping them.",
    "A's payers have an ops/compliance budget and sourced prices of $29–99/month for trackers, rising to $500–800/location/year with filing. B's sourced prices start at $12.90–19/month. That gives A more margin per customer and less pressure on volume.",
    "B's competitor evidence points against new-entrant traction. Descrii has 0 reviews, Gelo.ai has 3, and Describly has a single 1-star review. B's brief concludes that discovery, not building, is the bottleneck.",
    "A's live comparables, NeverFined at $29–99/month and ExpirationOps at $49/month or $490/year, show a thin tracking-only product with a disclaimer posture is a real offering at those prices. A's open questions also point to a narrowing path (one license type or industry) that B lacks against a free native tool."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "The ADA urgency claim in Idea B ($25,000–$75,000 settlements for missing alt text, and '77% of ADA lawsuits reportedly target online stores') comes from vendor marketing blogs (goodysell.com, compliapoint.com) that sell accessibility services, and the brief itself hedges with 'reportedly.' Of everything B offers as urgency to pay, as opposed to the free Shopify Magic option, this is the only piece, and it rests on self-interested secondary sources.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe saturated markets with no proven wedge, and both rely on a few Reddit quotes for demand. A has its own serious gaps. Its acquisition channel is costly paid search ($10–14.50 CPC) or already-contested SEO. Ongoing multi-state data maintenance is a real burden for one person. Neither brief gives traction data for A's small competitors. B has the advantage of a built-in App Store channel with low-cost ads, which could help land a first sale within 90 days. A wins mainly because it has no free native substitute, its need recurs, and its prices are higher, not because its evidence is strong."
}
```
